name: Nathan
overview: Nathan was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Zabud. His role as a priest situates him within the Levitical tradition of temple service and religious leadership. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nathan means "gift" in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God in the biblical text. It reflects a common Hebrew name without additional titles or meanings recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Nathan is identified as the father of Zabud, as mentioned in 1 Kings 4:5. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Nathan holds significance as a Levitical priest and the father of Zabud, linking him to the religious leadership during the time of Solomon. His presence in the biblical narrative underscores the importance of priestly families in supporting the organization of temple worship and royal administration. Although not detailed here, Nathan's broader role as a prophet during King David's reign highlights his commitment to uphold God's covenant and to speak truth to power.
